CurrentLocation: Archaeological Museum of Ancient Corinth, Corinth, Greece
Description: A Latin pavement inscription near Corinth's theatre reading that Erastus, in return for his aedileship, laid the pavement at his own expense. An aedile was a senior city official responsible for public works and finances.
BiblicalSignificance: Paul greets 'Erastus, the city treasurer' of Corinth in Romans 16:23, and many scholars identify the two as the same man, though the identification is debated because the titles differ slightly. Either way, the inscription shows a high-ranking Erastus in Paul's Corinth, illustrating how the gospel reached into civic leadership.
Interpretations: Scholars debate whether the Erastus named as Corinth’s aedile is Paul’s Erastus of Romans 16:23 — the name, city, and office fit, but the inscription does not prove the identification.
